dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?

Hello, Lorraine! Wonderful, somebody picked up! This is Diego Pagan, I'm calling about the road in front of my shop. It's a sheet of ice! A sheet! I've been trying to get somebody out here to sand it.
Okay, Mr. Pagan, I'm sorry about that. Let me get the details. Where is the shop located?
52 Thames Street! Fifth Ward, down toward the end, you know. Fifty-two. Great, you've got that?
Fifty-two Thames Street, got it. And you said the road is iced over, so that's the street itself and not just your sidewalk?

The street, the street! And the sidewalk edge too, but the street is the real problem. The plow came through, I'll give them that, but it scraped it and left a glaze. Nothing on it. No sand, no salt, nothing! Cars are sliding right through the stop. I watched a delivery van do a little dance this morning!
Oh, that's not good. So the plow went by, packed it down, and it froze into a glaze. Did that happen overnight?

Overnight, yes! The slush got pushed around yesterday afternoon, and then it all froze solid. And I'm up at five every morning to open, so I saw it first thing. I put down my own bag of ice melt by the door, but I can't do the whole street, Lorraine! I'm eighty-some years old!
No, of course not. You shouldn't have to. So what you're asking for is sand on the street in front of fifty-two Thames.
Sand! Yes, please, sand! Salt is fine too, great, whatever they have on the truck. But sand, I prefer sand, it grips right away. My customers come in and they're white-knuckled!
Understood. Let me write that down. Sand requested, fifty-two Thames Street, ice on the roadway after plowing. Is it a long stretch, or mostly right at your block?
It's the whole block, from the corner almost to the end. But the worst is right in front of me, there's a little dip where it sits. That's where the van did its dance!
Okay, the dip in front of your shop. I'll note that it's the worst spot. Has anyone been out since the plow went through?
Nobody! Not a soul! I called yesterday too, I left a message with some machine, and nobody called back. So here I am, calling again! It's the same story every winter, you call, you call, you call!
I'm sorry about the message going nowhere. I don't see a record of it here, so let's make sure this one gets in properly. Can I get a callback number in case the crew has a question?
Sure, sure! It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-six. That's the shop line, I'm there all day.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-six. Is that right?
That's it! Perfect! You repeat everything back, I like that!

Well, I'd rather get it right. Now, I can't promise an exact time, because the crews work down a priority list, main roads and hills first. But I'm sending this to the dispatcher as an icy road needing sand, and I'll flag that it's a business with people coming in and out.
Wonderful! But the priority list, Lorraine, I don't know. Thames Street is a main street! People park, people walk, tourists, all of that. It's not some back alley!

You're right, it's a busy one. I'll put that in the note too. When the truck comes, they'll usually do a pass with sand or a sand and salt mix. I'd expect it sometime today, but I don't want to name an hour.
Today, great. If it's today, I can live with it. I just don't want somebody falling! I have a lady who comes in every Thursday, she's seventy-eight, and she's due after lunch!
Then let's hope the truck beats her there. In the meantime, if you've got ice melt, keep putting it down by your entrance. And tell her to take her time on the walk.

I will, I will! I'll go out and meet her at the curb and hold her arm. Oh, and I have to run to the post office after this, I'm mailing a box of cookies to my sister's grandson in Ohio. Two dozen! I have to walk right across that ice to get to my car, so you see my interest!
Ha, well, then we really should get that sand out there. Please be careful on your way. Ohio's lucky.
They'd better like them! Anyway. So, who is going to come? Is it a city truck? Is it a contractor? Last year it was a fellow in a pickup, and he skipped us!
I don't know which truck will take it. It depends on who's on that route today. What I can do is put your number on the ticket so the dispatcher can reach you if it gets skipped.
Great! Put it on there. Put it big! Skipped, that's what I don't want to hear!
I'll make a note that this is a second request, since you called yesterday. That should push it up a little.
Second request, yes! Thank you! That's wonderful, Lorraine. Finally somebody who writes it down!

Let me read it back once more. Diego Pagan, fifty-two Thames Street, Fifth Ward. Ice on the street after plowing, worst in the dip in front of the shop. Requesting sand, second request. Callback four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-six. Did I miss anything?
No, that's all of it! That's exactly it! You should be running the whole department!
I don't think they'd let me. If nobody has come by the middle of the afternoon, call back and ask for me, and we'll push it again.
I will! Three o'clock, I'll be watching out the window. Thank you, thank you. Great job! Goodbye now!
You're welcome, Mr. Pagan. Watch your step out there. Goodbye.
